findings.problem: The either-direction substring matcher (normalized.includes(evidence) || evidence.includes(normalized)) can mis-attribute a short evidence sentence that is a common substring of the wrong role's line (e.g. a single shared token) to that earlier role. This only MIS-PLACES a kept bullet under a plausible-but-wrong role; it never drops or duplicates one, and the honesty gate is unaffected. Accepted as documented best-effort, but the bidirectional contains widens false-positive placement vs a directional or token-boundary match.
findings.fix: Optional hardening if placement fidelity matters later: require a minimum normalized-evidence length or word-boundary match before accepting the reverse (evidence.includes(line)) direction. Not required to ship; behavior is honest and covered.
